name: Firecamp
description: electron-updater with verifyUpdateCodeSignature:false, auto-download no prompt.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: In the reviewed Firecamp electron-builder configuration, the Windows target explicitly sets verifyUpdateCodeSignature to false. This records a Windows packaging/update-signature configuration boundary; runtime download policy and other platforms require separate evidence.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than the original study release; this review does not establish auto-download defaults, runtime invocation, or artifact behavior on macOS/Linux.

original_evidence.text: | Firecamp | github.com/firecamp-dev/firecamp — `packages/firecamp-electron` | Y (`electron-updater`) | Check: Y automatic — `appUpdater.checkForUpdate(false)` called on every window `ready-to-show` event at launch. Download: Y automatic — `autoUpdater.on('update-available', ...)` immediately calls `autoUpdater.downloadUpdate()` with no user prompt. Install: N automatic — `update-downloaded` shows a dialog; `quitAndInstall` only fires from that dialog (in `dialogs.ts`, not shown here but referenced). | Y | HTTPS — electron-builder `publish` targets GitHub Releases (`firecamp-dev/firecamp`) and DigitalOcean Spaces CDN | **N (explicitly disabled)** — `"verifyUpdateCodeSignature": false` is set in the Windows NSIS build config, turning off electron-updater's default Authenticode publisher-name verification step for Windows updates | none beyond an unsigned electron-builder-generated `latest*.yml` — hash-from-manifest (SHA-512, standard electron-builder output) is the only integrity check for Windows; the additional code-signature cross-check that electron-updater normally performs is explicitly turned off | n/a (no signature scheme relied upon for Windows since the check is disabled) | packages/firecamp-electron/src/updater/updater.ts:7 (`from 'electron-updater'`), :32-33 (`autoUpdater.autoDownload = false; autoUpdater.allowDowngrade = false;` — note: set on the object but overridden by immediate manual `downloadUpdate()` call below), :42 (`autoUpdater.downloadUpdate()` inside `update-available` handler — no user gate), :81 (`autoUpdater.checkForUpdatesAndNotify()`); packages/firecamp-electron/src/main.ts:73-75 (`win.on('ready-to-show', ...)` → `appUpdater.checkForUpdate(false)` — automatic startup check); packages/firecamp-electron/package.json:133 (`"verifyUpdateCodeSignature": false`), :76-90 (`publish: [{provider:"github",...}, {provider:"spaces",...}]`) | The explicit `verifyUpdateCodeSignature: false` on Windows is a genuine negative finding: it removes electron-updater's built-in Authenticode publisher-match check, leaving only the unsigned SHA-512 hash in `latest.yml` (itself fetched over HTTPS, so an attacker would need to compromise the HTTPS channel/host, but there's no additional signature layer as defense-in-depth). |
